completeSetup().details: Must be called by admin after deployment. Can only run once.      PolicyRegistry.setSentinelGate and ActivityLog.setWriter must      not have been called yet when this executes.

executePayment(bytes32,address,uint256,u.details: This is the only function that moves tokens. It runs the full      check sequence before touching any balances. If anything fails,      the entire transaction reverts — no partial state changes.      The calling pattern is: the agent's owner calls this on behalf      of the agent, or the agent itself calls it. Either way, the      policyId must match an active policy for the agent.

params.actionType: What kind of action this is.
params.amount: How much to send (in the policy's token).
params.policyId: The active policy governing this payment.
params.protocol: The protocol address for risk scoring (address(0) for agent-to-agent).

transferAdmin(address).details: The new admin must accept by being a non-zero address.      There is no two-step transfer here — keep that in mind      when choosing the admin address at deployment.

updateRiskGuardian(address).details: Used when oracle integrations are upgraded. The old address      is emitted so the change is fully traceable on-chain.

completeSetup().notice: Complete the one-time setup by registering this contract         as the authorised gate in PolicyRegistry and ActivityLog.

executePayment(bytes32,address,uint256,u.notice: Execute a payment on behalf of an agent.

transferAdmin(address).notice: Transfer admin rights to a new address.

updateRiskGuardian(address).notice: Replace the RiskGuardian with a new implementation.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (bytes32) view external returns (struct PolicyRegistry.Policy memory)

documentation.text:
@dev Write a blocked payment entry to the ActivityLog.
      Called before every revert so the block is always on record
      regardless of whether the outer transaction reverts.
      Note: because this is called before revert, and ActivityLog.writeEntry
      is a state change, we use a try/catch so a log failure never
      silently swallows the real revert reason.
